answer: BMR garbled circuits extend Yao to many parties who jointly garble the circuit, and the vertex of the construction is that no single party controls the garbling. The lantern of the design is a distributed oblivious transfer that delivers input labels without revealing choices, so a consortium can run an identity-uniqueness test together. A Sybil attacker would need to corrupt a majority of the garblers, and the pigment of the protocol makes each garbler's contribution independently verifiable.
